purpose.statement: EMPPAY is a standalone COBOL batch program that calculates an employee's weekly and monthly gross pay, applying overtime and performance reward rates, then displays the results to standard output. The program is authored by Ashis Kumar Naik and appears in the Open Mainframe Project COBOL Programming Course #4 (Testing) lab exercises.

code_references.snippet:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. EMPPAY.
       AUTHOR. ASHIS KUMAR NAIK.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM INITIALIZATION.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           PERFORM SHOW-OUTPUT.
           STOP RUN.

business_rules.statement: An employee's first name defaults to 'FRANCISCO' at the data-definition level, but is overridden to 'Millard' during initialization. The last name is set to 'Fillmore' during initialization. These values represent the employee whose pay is being computed.

code_references.snippet:
INITIALIZATION.
           MOVE "Millard"           TO EMP-FNAME.
           MOVE "Fillmore"          TO EMP-LNAME.
           MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

business_rules.statement: The standard working week is implicitly 40 hours. Hours worked per week and the hourly rate are hard-coded in the INITIALIZATION paragraph: 19 hours at $23.50 per hour.

code_references.snippet:
MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

business_rules.statement: Overtime rate business rule — Tier 1: If the employee works 40 or more hours in a week, an overtime multiplier of 0.25 (25%) is applied to the gross weekly pay calculation.

Overtime rate business rule — Tier 2: If the employee works 50 or more hours in a week, a higher overtime multiplier of 0.50 (50%) is applied. NOTE: Due to the ordering of the nested IF conditions, this branch is logically unreachable because the >= 40 condition will always be satisfied first when hours >= 50; this is a defect in the program logic.

code_references.snippet:
ELSE IF EMP-HOURS >= 50
               MOVE .50 TO EMP-OT-RATE

business_rules.statement: Overtime rate business rule — No overtime: If the employee works fewer than 40 hours in a week, no overtime premium applies and EMP-OT-RATE is set to zero.
Weekly gross pay is computed as: (Hours Worked × Hourly Rate) × (1 + Overtime Rate). This means the overtime rate acts as a percentage uplift on total pay rather than only on overtime hours.
Performance reward business rule: If the employee works more than 150 hours per week (monthly context implied), a reward multiplier of 0.50 (50%) is applied to the monthly pay.
No performance reward: If the employee does not exceed 150 hours, the reward rate is set to zero and no bonus uplift is applied to monthly pay.
Monthly gross pay is computed as: (Weekly Gross Pay × 4) × (1 + Reward Rate). The program assumes exactly 4 weeks per month and applies the reward as a percentage uplift on the total monthly figure.

inputs.statement: All input data is hard-coded in WORKING-STORAGE and the INITIALIZATION paragraph. There are no external files, databases, or user-supplied inputs. Employee name, hours worked (19), and hourly rate ($23.50) are the sole inputs.

code_references.snippet:
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       77  REC-COUNTER              PIC 9(1).
       01  EMP-RECORD.
           05  EMP-NAME.
                10 EMP-FNAME        PIC X(15) VALUE 'FRANCISCO'.
                10 EMP-LNAME        PIC X(15).
           05  EMP-HOURLY-RATE      PIC 9(3)V99.
           05  EMP-OT-RATE          PIC V99.
           05  EMP-REWARD           PIC V99.
           05  EMP-HOURS            PIC 9(3).
           05  EMP-PAY-WEEK         PIC 9(7)V99.
           05  EMP-PAY-MONTH        PIC 9(7)V99.

INITIALIZATION.
           MOVE "Millard"           TO EMP-FNAME.
           MOVE "Fillmore"          TO EMP-LNAME.
           MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

outputs.statement: The program's sole output is a series of DISPLAY statements written to standard output (SYSOUT/console). Output includes: employee full name, weekly hours worked, hourly rate, bonus/overtime rate, gross weekly pay, and gross monthly pay. A personal message is also displayed as the final line.

code_references.snippet:
SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".

processing_logic.statement: Step 1 — Initialization: The program begins by performing the INITIALIZATION paragraph, which populates employee name (Millard Fillmore), hours worked (19), and hourly rate (23.50) into WORKING-STORAGE fields.

code_references.snippet:
INITIALIZATION.
           MOVE "Millard"           TO EMP-FNAME.
           MOVE "Fillmore"          TO EMP-LNAME.
           MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

processing_logic.statement: Step 2 — Weekly Pay Calculation: The program performs PAYMENT-WEEKLY, which determines the overtime rate based on hours worked and then computes gross weekly pay using the formula (Hours × Rate) × (1 + OT-Rate).

code_references.snippet:
PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           IF  EMP-HOURS >= 40
               MOVE .25 TO  EMP-OT-RATE
           ELSE IF EMP-HOURS >= 50
               MOVE .50 TO EMP-OT-RATE
           ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-OT-RATE.
           COMPUTE EMP-PAY-WEEK =
                (EMP-HOURS * EMP-HOURLY-RATE) * (1 + EMP-OT-RATE).

processing_logic.statement: Step 3 — Monthly Pay Calculation: The program performs PAYMENT-MONTHLY, which determines the performance reward rate based on hours worked and then computes gross monthly pay as (Weekly Pay × 4) × (1 + Reward Rate).

code_references.snippet:
PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           IF  EMP-HOURS > 150
               MOVE .50 TO  EMP-REWARD
           ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-REWARD.
           COMPUTE EMP-PAY-MONTH =
                (EMP-PAY-WEEK * 4) * (1 + EMP-REWARD).

processing_logic.statement: Step 4 — Display Results: The program performs SHOW-OUTPUT, which displays all computed and input values to standard output, followed by a hard-coded personal message.

code_references.snippet:
SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".

processing_logic.statement: Step 5 — Program Termination: After all paragraphs have been performed, the program terminates normally via STOP RUN.

dependencies.statement: The program declares a working-storage counter field REC-COUNTER (PIC 9(1)) that is never initialized or referenced in the PROCEDURE DIVISION. This field may be a remnant from a template or a future-use placeholder, creating a latent dependency on a record-counting pattern that is not yet implemented.
The program has no external copybook, called subprogram, CICS transaction, DB2 table, MQ queue, or file dependency. It is entirely self-contained.

code_references.snippet:
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM INITIALIZATION.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           PERFORM SHOW-OUTPUT.
           STOP RUN.

error_handling.statement: The program contains no error-handling logic whatsoever: there are no ON SIZE ERROR clauses on the COMPUTE statements, no FILE STATUS checks, no EVALUATE for unexpected conditions, no abend handling, and no rollback mechanisms. Any arithmetic overflow (e.g., EMP-PAY-WEEK or EMP-PAY-MONTH exceeding PIC 9(7)V99) will produce silent truncation or a runtime abend depending on the platform.

downstream_effects.statement: The only downstream effect of this program is the text printed to standard output (SYSOUT/console). No files are written, no databases are updated, no messages are sent, and no other programs are called. The output is intended for human review as part of a COBOL course testing lab exercise.

SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".
